item.title: Buying a house in Canton Solothurn: prices and mortgage
item.description: Buying a home in the Canton of Solothurn requires careful financial planning. Learn how mortgage, equity, transfer tax, and notary fees work.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The purchase of a house is regulated by federal and cantonal regulations with a notarial procedure - Mortgage loan and own funds (20-30%) are essential for financing - Transfer tax and notary fees represent significant additional costs - The sustainability of the mortgage is assessed by the banks according to conservative standards
## Key facts - **What**: Real estate purchase in the Canton of Solothurn with federal and cantonal procedure - Where: Canton Solothurn, Switzerland, with registration in the cantonal land register - Who: Buyer, bank, notary, cantonal financial administration - Own funds: Typically 20-30% of the purchase price - Costs: Transfer tax (varies per canton), notary fees 0.5-1.5%, municipal taxes - Procedure: Offer → Mortgage application Banking → appraisal → Notary → Registration
Buying a home in the Canton of Solothurn requires careful financial planning and an understanding of different legal and tax aspects. In the Swiss real estate market, the procedure involves multiple actors: from the credit institution that provides the mortgage loan, to the notary that authenticates the transfer of ownership, to the cantonal authorities that collect the transfer tax. Switzerland is organized on three levels of taxation — federal, cantonal and municipal — and each applies its own rules on real estate. The main elements to be planned are the mortgage loan (main instrument of ### Transfer tax and notary fees: additional costs
Transfer tax (also known as real estate transfer tax, depending on cantonal terminology) is a cantonal tax applied to the transfer of real estate property between private individuals. It varies significantly from canton to canton: some cantons apply rates between 1% and 3% of the value of the sale, others reach 4-5%. In Canton Solothurn, as in other Swiss cantons, this tax is calculated on the basis of the purchase price or cadastral value, according to local regulations. It is essential to contact the Cantonal Administration of Finance of the Canton of Solothurn (or the competent tax office) to obtain precise and up-to-date figures, as the rates may vary and are sometimes differentiated according to the relationship between the parties (spouse, direct descendants, third parties). The municipalities of Soletta may also apply additional local sales taxes.
Notary fees are the fees due to the notary for the drafting, authentication and registration of the deed of sale with the land register. In Switzerland, notaries are regulated at cantonal level, which means that notary fees vary from canton to canton and sometimes even between municipalities. Generally, notary fees range from 0.5% to 1.5% of the purchase price, although this estimate must be verified directly with the competent notary in your
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Step-by-step procedure for buying a house in Solothurn
**Step 1 — Bank Prequalification**: Before you begin your active search, consult a bank or mortgage broker for a free prequalification. You will bring your last year's pay slip, your bank statement (demonstrating your available equity), and your tax declaration (federal IFD form, cantonal declaration from the canton of Solothurn or canton of residence). The bank will communicate the maximum mortgage amount you can obtain and the estimated monthly installments based on current SNB/SNB rates and your personal circumstances.
Step 2 — Search and Offer: Once you have identified the property, negotiate the price with the seller or real estate agent. Sign a binding offer (in some cantons called "promise to sell" or "offer to purchase"), which specifies the price, conditions and deadlines.
Step 3 — Formal mortgage application: Submit the official mortgage application to the bank, attaching the appraisal of the chosen property. The bank orders a professional appraisal to ensure that the value of the property adequately covers the loan (typically at least 80% of the appraisal value).
Phase 4 — Involvement of the notary: Once the mortgage has been approved, the notary draws up the deed of sale (or "sales contract"). It is at this stage that the transfer tax and notary fees are calculated and paid. The notary registers the transfer in the land registry of the Canton of Solothurn and manages the payments to the seller and the tax authorities.
Phase 5 — Mortgage disbursement and mortgage registration: Once the final checks have been completed, the bank disburses the mortgage via payment to the notary or directly into the account. The mortgage is registered in the land register of the Canton of Solothurn, guaranteeing the bank the right of lien on the property if the borrower does not pay the installments.
### Essential documents to prepare
Prepare a folder immediately with: - Last 2 years of pay slips and tax returns (federal and cantonal) - Recent bank statements (proof of savings for own funds) - Certificate of good conduct (required by some banks) - Letter of employment or employment contract (with indication of duration and stability) - Declaration of activity and income (if self-employed or freelancer) - Proof of additional financing (if you receive help from family members - banks often require a "gift" declaration with no obligation to repay) - Ownership documentation of other properties (if applicable)
### Practical tools and resources
Consult the official website of the Cantonal Finance Administration of the Canton of Solothurn for the updated transfer tax rates and the specific municipal taxes of your municipality of interest. Contact a notary active in the Canton of Solothurn directly to receive a written estimate of specific notary fees based on the price of your property. Use a [calcolatore di mutuo](nav:calculator) to estimate your monthly payments based on your reported income, current interest rates and the loan amount you are requesting. Consult the websites of the main Swiss banks (UBS, Credit Suisse, Raiffeisen, Migros Bank, PostFinance) or mortgage brokers such as Comparis to compare interest rates on mortgages and find the best conditions. Regularly monitor the SNB/SNB decisions on key rates, as they directly influence your future mortgage interest costs.
### Final action
The next concrete step: contact a bank today for a free, no-obligation prequalification. Also ask the municipal administration of your municipality of interest in the canton of Solothurn for information regarding municipal property taxes and any other local taxes. This data will allow you to carefully plan the purchase and evaluate the financial sustainability of the mortgage in the long term, ensuring that the mortgage payment remains sustainable even in a scenario of rising rates.

## In a nutshell - Child custody in Switzerland is the responsibility of the cantons - Nurseries, day families and after-school are the main services - Rates calculated on the scale graduated according to family income - Cantonal subsidies available for low- and middle-income families

Childcare in Switzerland is a primary responsibility of the cantons. Each canton organizes and regulates custodial services, defining access criteria, fees and financial contributions for families. This decentralised system mirrors the federal structure of Switzerland, where important competences in the social field fall to the cantons.
Childcare services fall into three main categories: kindergartens for young children (generally up to 4-5 years old), day families caring for children in their homes (more flexible alternative to kindergartens), and afterschool for school-age children. The range and availability of these services vary by canton: some have an extensive network of public facilities, ### How cantonal fares and subsidies work
Rates in custodial services are structured with an income-inclusive approach. Many cantons use the net income of the family as the basis of calculation, applying a percentage that varies according to the income group. This means that a family that earns modest amounts pays less than one that earns more.
The graduated pricing model pursues a dual objective: to ensure that childcare services remain financially sustainable while at the same time ensuring that families with limited economic resources are not excluded. Some cantons also provide additional reductions for families with multiple children in custody simultaneously.
### Cantonal subsidies and access
The cantons offer direct subsidies to families, mainly aimed at those with low-middle income. These subsidies can cover a significant percentage of the living expenses, sometimes up to 50% or more, depending on the economic situation. To access benefits, families generally need to submit a tax return and documentation of their family situation. Exact criteria for access vary by canton, as do income limits and maximum grant amounts.
